function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content: Electricity isn’t the discovery of a single person—it’s a natural phenomenon that has been observed and studied for millennia.  Early Greek philosophers like Thales noted static electricity from rubbing amber.  In the 17th‑18th centuries, scientists such as William Gilbert, Otto von Guericke, and later Benjamin Franklin (who coined the terms “positive” and “negative”) made systematic observations.  The modern understanding began to take shape with Alessandro Volta’s invention of the voltaic pile (the first battery), Luigi Galvani’s work on bioelectricity, and Michael Faraday’s discoveries of electromagnetic induction.  So, rather than a single discoverer, electricity emerged through the cumulative efforts of many thinkers over centuries.
